verdicts.rationale: Two halves, neither passes the purpose test. (a) The +4s Aurous Blaze duration extension modifies Aurous Blaze, which is itself unmodeled — the burst ships effects:[] with no summon entry, so there is no rendered window for a duration extension to diverge from. (b) The +20% ATK-for-20s self-buff is gated on enemy death (onTargetDied), a null-resolving game state the tool does not simulate, sitting in the same out-of-scope bucket as pickup-driven mechanics; there is no wired trigger primitive for it and it was intentionally deferred under the stub-with-caveat philosophy. A kill-gated buff also cannot drive rotation choices (you cannot plan around a kill), so it is not decision-relevant, and the timeline showing nothing is the honest default rather than a misleading divergence. Not implementable, not add.
rubricRefs: CANNOT model: onTargetDied enemy-death null-resolving trigger
no rendered surface to diverge from

verdicts.rationale: This constellation is fully authored and renders: a self pyroDmgBonus 25 buff, 6s refresh, onHit filtered on pyro+isCrit. The only divergence is that the isCrit filter fires optimistically, treating every pyro hit as a potential crit — the standard optimistic-render pattern, and the curator note itself calls the filter a schema-fidelity declaration rather than a real limitation. For a crit-focused Pyro DPS the assumed crit is essentially always true, so the optimistic window matches practical reality and does not mislead. Describing the optimistic auto-fire would be documenting working behavior, which the style guide says to delete, not caveat.
rubricRefs: optimistic-fire is working behavior — never describe working behavior

groundedIn.quote: When Yoimiya's Pyro DMG scores a CRIT Hit, Yoimiya will gain a 25% Pyro DMG Bonus for 6s.

groundedIn.claim: The isCrit filter fires optimistically as a schema-fidelity declaration, not a modeled limitation.
groundedIn.quote: The renderer's optimistic-fire isCrit semantics treat every hit as a potential crit (filter v1 caveat); the filter primarily serves as a schema-fidelity declaration.

verdicts.rationale: This constellation is a probabilistic extra Normal-Attack arrow dealing 60% of its DMG — a pure damage-add. It adds no separate action and no frame timing (it fires as part of the Normal Attack and is counted as Normal Attack DMG), so there is no rendered timeline surface to diverge from. Damage numbers and math are constitution-excluded, and there is no probabilistic-damage primitive, so it is neither implementable nor decision-relevant to rotation planning.
rubricRefs: no rendered surface / no timing change

groundedIn.quote: Probabilistic extra-hit mechanic: 50% chance per in-stance N for an extra arrow at 60% of total mult. Not modeled — schema has no probabilistic damage-add concept and proc reliability is non-trivial in practice.
